title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten admission-free places and activities at James Madison University, with public and student-only access clearly distinguished.

cards.title: Walk the Arboretum Trails
cards.subtitle: A free dawn-to-dusk loop through JMU’s public garden
cards.notes: Meet at the Frances Plecker Education Center, choose a trail around the pond, and leave plants, wildlife, and natural materials undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: Take an unhurried group walk through the arboretum’s gardens, woods, streams, and pond landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU states that the Edith J. Carrier Arboretum grounds are free to the public and open from dawn to dusk every day of the year.
cards.access_notes: Public access; grounds are open dawn to dusk, 365 days a year. Follow posted rules, including no fishing, feeding ducks, or group sports on the lawn.

cards.title: Catch a Saturday Planetarium Show
cards.subtitle: Free full-dome programs and a live Valley-sky talk
cards.notes: Bring friends to Miller Hall and arrive before the listed showtime; seating is limited, but the public needs neither admission payment nor a ticket.
cards.short_summary: Share a full-dome astronomy feature followed by a live look at the season’s stars and constellations.
cards.evidence_claim: The planetarium’s official schedule says its Saturday public shows offer free admission to the public and require no tickets.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public on scheduled Saturdays; consult the current schedule and JMU break closures. No ticket is needed, and seating is first come.

cards.title: Compare Crystals at the Mineral Museum
cards.subtitle: A free group browse through JMU’s geoscience collection
cards.notes: Plan a visit after regular hours resume, then compare specimens together; groups needing special timing should arrange a tour with museum staff.
cards.short_summary: Turn the mineral cases into a low-key visual scavenger hunt for colors, structures, and formations.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU lists admission to the Mineral Museum as free and offers visitors a free parking-pass option through Parking Services.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit to the Mineral Museum - JMU
cards.access_notes: The museum is closed for construction and relocation through August 24, 2026; JMU anticipates regular hours resuming August 26. Confirm reopening before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Duke Hall Gallery of Fine Art
cards.title: Trade Takes on a Gallery Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Free public exhibitions in Duke Hall
cards.notes: Visit with a small group during academic-year hours, choose one work each to discuss, and contact gallery staff ahead for groups larger than 35.
cards.short_summary: Use a rotating contemporary-art exhibition as the starting point for an informal group conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official visitor page states that its exhibitions are always free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: About Duke Hall Gallery of Fine Art - JMU
cards.access_notes: Public access during exhibitions. Academic-year hours are Tuesday through Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; the gallery is closed in summer. Verify the current exhibition calendar.

cards.title: Browse the Madison Art Collection
cards.subtitle: A ticketless art stop on West Grace Street
cards.notes: Drop in with classmates during public hours, compare favorite pieces, or ask staff in advance whether a guided group tour can be arranged.
cards.short_summary: Spend an afternoon examining collection displays without buying admission or reserving a ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: The Madison Art Collection says it is free and open to all visitors and that its exhibitions are never ticketed, including group visits.
cards.source_title: Madison Art: Frequently Asked Questions - JMU
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Tuesday through Friday, noon–4 p.m. Group visits do not require advance notice, although tours depend on staff availability.

cards.title: Read Poetry Through Visual Art
cards.subtitle: Free rotating broadside exhibitions at JMU
cards.notes: Bring a friend, read the displayed poems aloud or silently, and compare how each broadside’s visual design changes your response to the words.
cards.short_summary: Explore the meeting point of poetry and visual art through signed and limited-edition broadsides.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s Furious Flower Poetry Center states that the Broadside Gallery is free and open to the public and rotates exhibits about every other month.
cards.source_title: Class Visits to the Furious Flower Broadside Gallery - JMU
cards.access_notes: Free public access; independent and class visits are welcomed. Contact the Poetry Center to confirm the current location, exhibit, and available visiting hours.

cards.title: Swap Seeds at the Community Seed Library
cards.subtitle: A self-service sharing activity with no library card needed
cards.notes: Browse the seed drawers together, take only what you can grow, and return labeled seeds later so the shared collection continues serving the community.
cards.short_summary: Plan a garden project with friends using JMU Libraries’ community seed-sharing collection.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU Libraries identifies the Community Seed Library as a self-service seed-sharing library available to everyone with no library card necessary.
cards.source_title: Services for Visitors and Alumni - JMU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available to all visitors during the host library’s operating hours; no library card is required. Check current library locations and hours before going.

cards.title: Take a Quiet Reset in the Oasis
cards.subtitle: A free student relaxation space in the Counseling Center
cards.notes: Bring your JACard, check in at the Counseling Center front desk, and share a quiet decompression break while respecting the room’s restorative purpose.
cards.short_summary: Pause together between classes in a student self-care room equipped with relaxation resources.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s Counseling Center says the Oasis is free for students to use after checking in with a JACard and notes that it includes massage chairs.
cards.source_title: Counseling Center: Campus Wellness Resources - JMU
cards.access_notes: Current JMU students only. Check in with a JACard at the Counseling Center front desk in Student Success Center, third floor, Suite 3100.

cards.title: Make Art Together in the Studio
cards.subtitle: Free student art supplies for a casual creative break
cards.notes: Check in with your JACard, pick a simple project everyone can try, and return shared supplies neatly when your low-pressure art session ends.
cards.short_summary: Gather for an informal creative session using the Counseling Center’s provided art materials.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU’s Counseling Center states that the Studio supplies art materials and is free for students to use after checking in with a JACard.
cards.source_title: Counseling Center: Campus Wellness Resources - JMU
cards.access_notes: Current JMU students only. Check in with a JACard at the Counseling Center front desk in Student Success Center, third floor, Suite 3100.

cards.title: Start a Pick-Up Game at University Park
cards.subtitle: Student courts, fields, and equipment without an extra fee
cards.notes: Swipe in with your JACard, choose pickleball, tennis, basketball, or another available activity, and check out shared equipment if your group needs it.
cards.short_summary: Turn an open court or field into a spontaneous game using equipment included for eligible members.
cards.evidence_claim: JMU says students have UREC membership, may play pick-up sports at University Park during operating hours, and can check out equipment at no extra cost.
cards.access_notes: Current JMU students and other eligible UREC members must swipe a JACard or use the UREC app. Facility access and equipment checkout are included; verify operating hours.
